tldr: OpenAI has made the case for GPT-5.6 Sol with product moves rather than benchmarks: a Model ML finance case study on Aug 10, then a Cerebras-powered Ultrafast API tier on Aug 13 claiming up to 750 output tokens per second. Both the capability and the speed figures are OpenAI-reported.
whats_new: A tech-insider.org comparison on Aug 19 reframes Sol against Claude Opus 5 and Qwen 3.8 Max around a claimed 4x price gap — the first non-OpenAI input in this thread, and it grades on price, not capability.
why_it_matters: Every Sol performance claim on the table is vendor-sourced, and the one outside datapoint is a price listicle — so a platform engineer choosing between Sol, Opus 5, and Qwen 3.8 Max still has no independent eval to weigh against the cost delta.

status.state: Unbenchmarked · vendor claims plus one price listicle
status.detail: Sol's case is carried by two OpenAI posts (a finance case study and the Ultrafast speed tier); the only third-party input so far compares price, not capability.

beats.headline: OpenAI publishes a finance case study: Sol turns research into traceable decks and workbooks
beats.summary: Model ML's story has Sol carrying finance research through to editable PowerPoint and Excel output — a deployment data point, not a benchmark.

beats.headline: Ultrafast preview runs Sol at up to 14X speed on Cerebras
beats.summary: A new API service tier claims up to 750 output tokens per second, moving OpenAI's argument for Sol from quality to throughput.

beats.headline: Third-party listicle puts a 4x price gap across Sol, Qwen 3.8 Max, and Claude Opus 5
beats.summary: The first outside voice in the thread competes on price rather than capability, leaving Sol's quality and speed claims still uncorroborated.

open_questions: Is the tech-insider.org 4x price gap built from official list pricing for all three models, or from mismatched plans and tiers?
Does the Ultrafast tier's 14X / 750 tok-per-sec figure hold in an independent latency benchmark?
What does Ultrafast cost — does the Cerebras-backed tier carry a price premium that changes the 4x gap?
Does the Model ML case study's 'traceable' output claim survive third-party review, or does it stay a customer story OpenAI published?
Does any independent agentic or coding benchmark rank Sol against Qwen 3.8 Max and Claude Opus 5?
take_for_builders: Before committing to Sol on price, pull the official rate cards for all three models yourself — including whatever Ultrafast costs — and run your own latency and quality eval; the 14X speed number is OpenAI's and the 4x gap comes from an aggregator, not a vendor price page.
